title: 22nd sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with 52 members present, passed the minutes of sittings 16 to 18 and heard that members would vote later on seats for a new Housing committee. Most of the part was the opening debate on a government bill to change the Local Councils Elections Act so by-elections for vacant council seats are held twice a year, between 120 and 183 days apart, instead of within 60 days. Members from both sides argued about cost, low turnout, e-voting and council size, and the debate closed with the vote left for the day's voting time. After the break the House heard that a committee approved Ismail Habeeb for the Human Rights Commission, then began the debate on a bill amending the Employment Act, which is cut off mid-speech at the end of this part. This part continues the debate on the bill to amend the Employment Act (2008/2), which mostly concerns caps and rules for bringing in foreign workers. Members raised worries about unregulated migration, absconding workers, fines on employers, a 30-day paid sick leave rule and the black market for dollars, while several said the bill is a good step. After the break at 11:49 the sitting resumed at 13:00 with four votes: a housing committee membership motion, the Local Councils Elections Act amendment, the appointment of a Human Rights Commission member, and the Employment Act bill, which was accepted 79-0 and sent to the Security Services committee.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Told the chair how he voted after a voting-machine fault: supported the HRC appointment and the acceptance of the Employment Act bill.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said electronic voting could cut by-election costs and that dropping by-elections would set back democratic practice.
Raised concern about low youth interest in voting and argued the government's reasoning about costs was weak.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Argued decentralisation has not delivered results for citizens and cited low turnout in Male' by-elections as support for the change.
Calls migration a national-level concern, citing the dollar black market and migrant networks in trade and food supply.
Raises worry about cultural change but regards the bill as a good one.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the bill and spoke on decentralisation, local resource sharing and the history of council elections.
On the Employment Act bill, voiced concern about the proposed MVR 50,000 fine on employers and said foreign worker rules are poorly enforced.

speakers.name: Munthazim Ibrahim
positions: Introduced the bill: hold by-elections for vacant council seats twice a year, 120 to 183 days apart, instead of within 60 days, to cut election costs.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Raised a point of order that statements attributed to the President were false and against the rules; the chair ruled it was not a point of order.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the bill, saying frequent elections strain government and parties and holding elections together would help.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill but asked that the committee consider how councils with changed structure, such as Thinadhoo moving to a city council, are treated.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said the bill is not only about cost, pointing to low by-election turnout and councils losing a quorum when seats stay empty.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the bill and argued councillors need better pay and allowances so fewer resign and fewer by-elections are needed.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill as national work and responded to opposition criticism of the government's reasons.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the bill, said by-election money could fund services, and opposed introducing e-voting.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Supported the bill, reviewing the constitution's decentralisation chapter and past changes to council numbers and election timing.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Raised concern that Addu City ward seats could sit vacant for months without a councillor under the new timing.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Supported fewer by-elections but asked why council elections are not held together with presidential and parliamentary elections.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Presented the committee report recommending Ismail Habeeb Abdulrahman for the Human Rights Commission after an interview scored 89%.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: On the Employment Act bill, expressed concern about foreign worker quotas being moved to ministry control; speech continues beyond this part.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supports much of the bill but questions a flat MVR 50,000 fine per employee, saying costs fall on local businesses, and urges the committee to revisit it.
Wants a defined window for reporting absconding workers and doubts deportation alone solves the problem.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Backs the bill, saying 2022 figures show a Bangladeshi worker count that could not be monitored; quotas should follow job-market studies.
Asks the committee to let businesses with several outlets use workers across sites and to reconsider 30 days of paid sick leave.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Says unregulated migration is a major problem and laws are written without looking at conditions on the ground.
Asks for regulation of recruitment agencies and enforceable rules on insurance and absconding workers.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Supports setting administrative fees by regulation and keeping the cap on workers from one country.
Argues the aim is to bring irregular workers into the rules and that Maldivians should take up jobs.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 2024/16 to 2024/18 accepted by the chair.
Debate on the Local Councils Elections Act amendment bill concluded; vote set for the day's voting time.
Debate on the Human Rights Commission nominee report concluded without speakers; vote set for the day's voting time.
Vote on electing members to the Housing committee set for the day's voting time.
Local Councils Elections Act amendment bill accepted 77-0-0 and sent to the Decentralisation committee.
Ismail Habeeb Abdul Rahim's appointment to the Human Rights Commission approved 74-3.
Employment Act amendment bill accepted 79-0-0 and sent to the Security Services committee.
Next sitting set for Monday 5 August 2024 at 09:00.
